pageCache.pageTitle: British Values - Holy Trinity CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values
The UK government outlined 4 key British values to be taught and embedded into the fabric of every school. Each of these values are taught both explicitly and implicitly. They are woven into the daily running of school life at Holy Trinity. The 4 key values are explained below.
Democracy
Democracy is present through our Infant and Junior leadership teams. Children from each class can put themselves forward for a vote by their class. The leadership teams meet monthly with a teacher to raise any issues and share ideas. The role is able to effect change in our school and hear perspectives from the pupil’s voice. Children are encouraged to see their ideas being listened to and how their ideas can be a force for positive improvement in school life.
The Rule of Law
The importance of laws, whether they are those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced at Holy Trinity. From Reception, Each school year starts with looking at the rules that keep us safe in our classrooms and school. This is then referring to throughout the year. Our school values are also spoken about in a positive way and modelled all the way through the school community, particularly celebrating our values champions each week.
Individual Liberty
At Holy Trinity, we celebrate that every child is unique and has the power to make their own choices with the support of the clear boundaries and routines that are established into the life of the school. We value children making informed choices through lessons that are engaging and explore the decisions children have to make right from Reception .Whether this is the choice of what to eat for at hot lunch times to how to keep ourselves safe on the street and on line. These lessons are taught through our PSHE curriculum which occur weekly.
Mutual Respect
Our school vision of Love learning, love another and love God cultivates an enriching environment for children to thrive in respecting each other. Respect is taught explicitly through how we show value to the words we say to each other in class times and in the playground. In circle times in PSHE, we build upon the importance of listening to a range of ideas and views and how we can support each other’s thought. During our PSHE lessons, RE lessons and collective worship times, we teach and model mutual respect and also take this attitude to all areas of school life including staff as well as pupils.
At Holy Trinity, we are proud to be a diverse school of different views and beliefs. We encourage different views and faiths to be respectfully explored in class discussions in PSHE and RE lessons. We partake in different multicultural activities throughout the year and visit different places of worship. We are pleased that through our school values we are able to love one another regardless of differences we may have.
Love, Aspiration, Community

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Reception at Holy Trinity School
We have so much fun in our Reception class and love learning!
We follow a play-based curriculum that nurtures independent, curious and active learners who love to explore, take risks and rise to challenges. We build strong foundations through hands-on experiences that follow the interests of the children, preparing them with confidence for their learning journey. As OFSTED commented “Children in Early Years get off to a flying start.”
Early Years Foundation Stage
The ‘Early Years Foundation Stage’ (EYFS) is the statutory curriculum, covering the learning and development from birth to five. At Holy Trinity, we value the importance that the EYFS plays in laying secure foundations for future learning and development. Learning through play is key to the development of young children and we provide rich, creative learning opportunities that capture children’s interest, engaging and motivating them to develop skills through a graduated approach.
Our school values
We value each child as a unique individual and by providing rich and engaging learning experiences, aim to ignite a lifelong love of learning and equip them with the tools and knowledge to fulfil their potential. In keeping with our Christian foundation, we nurture the values of aspiration, love and community and encourage the children to discover and develop their gifts and talents so that they can make a positive contribution to the world around them.
Learning through play
In our setting we follow a child centred approach and explore using our continuous provision. Throughout each half term, we have different topics to explore, alongside small adult led groups and our free-flow learning. We cover all areas of the Early Years curriculum and ensure the children leave reception full of amazing memories and feeling confident and ready to continue their learning into Key Stage 1.
Admissions
Children born between 1st September 2022 and 31st August 2023 are due to start reception class at primary school in September 2027. The deadline for applications for places in September 2027 is on 15th January 2026. Further details regarding admissions at Holy Trinity School can be found here:
Please use this form for details of dates and to book a tour
If you would like to apply for a September 2027 place and would like help or require a tour of our school please use this google form to book your place We would be delighted to show you our wonderful school.
Love, Aspiration, Community

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Holy Trinity
Dear Families, Friends, and Visitors,
It is our absolute pleasure to welcome you to Holy Trinity. Whether you’re a prospective parent, a new family joining us, or simply exploring who we are, we’re delighted to open our doors to you and share a glimpse of what makes our school such a special place to be.
At Holy Trinity, you’ll find a vibrant, nurturing environment where every child is truly known and valued. We are proud of our strong, inclusive ethos, built on compassion, respect, and a deep commitment to helping children flourish in every aspect of their lives.
We place an emphasis on academic excellence, and our dedicated staff work hard to ensure every child is challenged, supported, and inspired to achieve their very best. Our classrooms are filled with curiosity, creativity, and high expectations—and we celebrate progress, perseverance, and a love of learning.
But education at Holy Trinity goes far beyond the classroom. We are passionate about sport and physical activity, encouraging children to stay active, build resilience, and enjoy being part of a team. Whether it’s through PE lessons, local tournaments, or after-school clubs, we believe sport plays a vital role in developing healthy, confident learners.
Music is another cornerstone of our school life. From joyful singing in assemblies to learning instruments, performing in school productions, or joining our choir, we offer children many opportunities to discover their musical gifts and experience the joy of performance and self-expression.
While we are proud of our Christian heritage, we warmly welcome children and families of all backgrounds. Our shared values of Apiration, Love and Community help shape the way we treat one another and the way we care for our wider community, helping to build a school culture rooted in kindness, integrity, and inclusion.
Above all, Holy Trinity is a place of belonging—a school where friendships are made, talents are discovered, and children grow not only in knowledge but in character.
We are so glad you’re here. Thank you for taking the time to get to know us. We look forward to welcoming you in person and sharing the exciting journey ahead with you and your child.
With heartfelt best wishes, Maryanne Boon Headteacher
Our Vision Our Values
As a Church of England school, our vision and values are rooted in the Christian faith and the teaching of the Bible. They shape everything that we do and the way that we do it, day by day.
Our vision is that children are nurtured to love learning, love one another and love God.
We take our inspiration from Jesus’ words in John 10:10:
“I have come so that you might have life – life in all its fullness.”
These words offer us a picture of what it is to flourish, and we want every child at Holy Trinity to experience life in all its fullness, academically, socially, and spiritually.
We live out our vision through three core values, which we hope every member of our community can understand and put into practice.
ASPIRATION
‘Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord.’ (Colossians 3:23)
Aspiration means doing our best, aiming high and believing that we can grow. We show aspiration through resilience, creativity, perseverance and courage.
LOVE
‘We love because God first loved us.’ (1 John 4:19)
Love is at the heart of the Christian and faith and at the heart of our school. We show love through compassion, truth, kindness and forgiveness.
COMMUNITY
‘Welcome one another as Christ has welcomed you.’ (Romans 15:7)
Community means belonging, supporting one another and working together. We show this value through inclusivity, friendship, respect and responsibility.
Love, Aspiration, Community

We take our inspiration from Jesus’ words in John 10:10:
“I have come so that you might have life – life in all its fullness.”
These words offer us a picture of what it is to flourish, and we want every child at Holy Trinity to experience life in all its fullness, academically, socially, and spiritually.
We live out our vision through three core values, which we hope every member of our community can understand and put into practice.
ASPIRATION
‘Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord.’ (Colossians 3:23)
Aspiration means doing our best, aiming high and believing that we can grow. We show aspiration through resilience, creativity, perseverance and courage.
LOVE
‘We love because God first loved us.’ (1 John 4:19)
Love is at the heart of the Christian and faith and at the heart of our school. We show love through compassion, truth, kindness and forgiveness.
COMMUNITY
‘Welcome one another as Christ has welcomed you.’ (Romans 15:7)
Community means belonging, supporting one another and working together. We show this value through inclusivity, friendship, respect and responsibility.
Love, Aspiration, Community

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Kingfisher Class - Holy Trinity CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Kingfisher class at Holy Trinity School
Through play and active learning our pupils reach their begin their learning journey in an ASPIRING and visually rich environment, that encourages creative and critical thinking. During this year our pupils will explore the seven areas of learning set out by the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS).
Communication & Language
Speaking Listening, Attention, Understanding
Through stories, songs and poems we give the children the opportunity to experience a rich language environment. It’s a time for the children to explore listening, learning to be attentive, answer and ask questions. We share our thoughts and ideas together.
Personal, Social & Emotional Development
Building relationships, Self regulation, Personal management
In this area of learning we help the children to understand their own feelings and the feelings of others. How to form friendships and positive attachments and cooperative play. We do this with circle time, sharing our news, modelling expectations using puppets and role play. We encourage a “can do” attitude and use the Zones of Regulation to help our children communicate their feelings.
We spend time helping our children continue to improve their understanding of their personal needs and personal hygiene.
Physical Development
Fine motor, Gross motor,
The Kingfisher classroom is designed to excite and encourage our learners in their physical development. With its own outdoor learning area, it is an excellent continuation of the classroom providing children with the opportunity and space to explore their physical capabilities. An integral part of the day is physical activity including dancing, jumping, wiggling, climbing, scooting, Each of these playful experiences helps our children to have confidence in their spacial awareness.
Each day there are number of activities that encourage fine motor skills required for holding a pencil and mark making, using small tools and improving accuracy.
Mathematics
Number Numerical Patterns
We help our children become fluent in numbers 1 to 10 and beyond, using a Maths Mastery approach following the curriculum set by the National Center of Excellence in The Teaching of Mathematics.
Through active learning the children cement their understanding of number bonds, subtraction facts, doubling and sharing through active learning and role play.
Literacy
Comprehension, Word Reading, Writing
Following Read Write Inc, we use the phonics to give our pupils the tools to read and write simple sentences. Care is take to develop their mark making skills to write recognisable letters, spell words and write phrases.
Using a carefully selected range of books that show the children a diverse community of characters, we can inspire their minds and writing.
Understanding the World
People, Culture, Communities, Natural World, The Past and Present.
Through active learning and hands on experiences, our children explore the world around them. Talking about the people they know and the the people they meet.
It is important our children can identify similarities and differences in the past and present as well as the religions and cultures they will experience in our global community.
With regular access to our Forest School our children can explore nature whilst problem solving simple tasks like den building. In a safe an nurturing environment.
Expressive Art & Design
Being imaginative, Expressive, Creating with materials.
Role play, music, art and signing are creative outlets to help our children express themselves and develop their personalities. Exploring textures, materials and tools the children can problem solve and communicate visually with their friends, an introduction to creative thinking.
It provides an excellent opportunity for collaborative learning.
STEM in Reception
Being Inquisitive, Practical learning, Developing language.
Our goal is to encourage curiosity, practical skills, and relevant language development to inspire young learners in STEM.
We encourage our children to ask questions, with the support of their peers and our teachers to find the answers. This can be using their interests to conduct experiments resulting in hands-on discovery.
STEM topics provide an excelent environment to introduce specific vocabulary, allowing children to develop their language skills. Role playing as engineers, architects, builders, chemists, astrologists can help children learn about the world around them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages - Holy Trinity CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Foreign Languages
Languages progression of skills
Intent
EYFS and KS1: Celebration of Languages
In Early Years and KS1 we introduce our children to language. We share and celebrate all the different languages that are spoken in and amongst our community. We share and enjoy the different celebrations and festivals that our relevant and important to our community.
At Holy Trinity School, we have chosen as a community to teach Latin as it provides a linguistic foundation for reading comprehension and broadens children’s views of the wider world. Latin is not only still used in many aspects of the English language, but is also seen as the blueprint for some of the most widely spoken languages today, many of which are spoken by children at Holy Trinity School. We want pupils to have access to a progressive and cohesive curriculum where they can use Latin to gain a deeper understanding of grammatical structures, vocabulary and etymology. We want our children to show the values of aspiration and love of learning a language and to appreciate classical civilisations and the impact they have had on modern society.
Implementation
Although not statutory, we are passionate that our children in EYFS and KS1 have opportunities to be learn about the different languages spoken within our community and our diverse, wider world. We want our children to foster a love for languages linked to their heritage and recognise the connections between languages and etymology. This will prepare the pupils for learning a language in KS2.
Latin at Holy Trinity School is taught to KS2 pupils using the acclaimed “Minimus” scheme of work – a lively introduction to Latin for children in KS2 authored by Cambridge classics scholar, Barbara Bell. The scheme provides a fascinating introduction to Roman culture and basic Latin language skills. Lessons are a mix of myths, stories, role play, grammar support and historical background. There are opportunities for children to take part in simple Latin exchanges throughout KS2.
Impact
The learning of Latin at Holy Trinity School provides children with the same educational opportunities as their peers in independent schools. Teachers work closely with the children during lessons and provide effective formative assessment and feedback in small groups or pairs. Many of the activities focus on verbal exchanges where pupils practise the key learning with their peers. Lessons are broken down into chapters that progress and build upon prior knowledge. Written work and key vocabulary is also often recorded and can be presented in the classroom. Progress checks are used at the end of every 4th chapter to see how pupils are tracking. Termly learning walks and ‘Pupil voices’ are also used to ensure children are making progress in their learning.
Love, Aspiration, Community

Science
Science Progression Map of Skills
Intent
At Holy Trinity School we want to inspire every child to develop a love of science through active and engaging learning that is relevant to their everyday lives and experiences. We aim to create independent learners who aspire to success and are adept at applying their knowledge and skills to solving real world community problems.
Our curriculum follows the National Curriculum for primary science, while maximising our unique resources including the STEM Hub and our outdoor learning area. Our science curriculum is lead by Mrs Lambert, a Fellow of the PSTT Teaching College, recognised for her dedication to science in the classroom. Holy Trinity School is proud to have been awarded the Primary Science Quality Mark again under her excellent leadership.
Implementation
Our curriculum is organised into the three scientific disciplines: biology, chemistry and physics. Working scientifically skills are woven into every lesson and are taught alongside scientific knowledge. To support this we have a fantastic array of resources in our STEM Hub – a space dedicated to the delivery of STEM subjects, and especially science. The children are taught to use equipment such as microscopes and data loggers, and are able to choose from a range of up-to-date and engaging resources when working scientifically.

Children spend one afternoon per week learning science, and some of these lessons will be taught in the Hub.
Outdoor learning is embedded into our science curriculum. Our wildlife garden, pond, and eco-area are used regularly to support, enhance and enrich our children’s learning experiences. Alongside the use of our own school site, we also make good use of local sites such as Richmond Park, including Holly Lodge, Kew Gardens and Sheen Common.

pageCache.text:
Art & Design
Art and Design Progression Map
Intent
At Holy Trinity School, we value Art and Design as an integral part of a child’s entitlement to a broad, balanced and interesting curriculum. Art and Design provides our children with opportunities to develop and extend skills and the chance to creatively express their individual interests, thoughts and ideas across a range of mediums. Our curriculum has been designed to expose learners to a variety of different artists and designers from a range of cultures, communities and historical periods.
Implementation
The key skills that the curriculum promotes are built upon from EYFS and through KS1 and KS2. The expectations and outcomes become progressively more sophisticated and challenging as time goes on. During their time at Holy Trinity School, a child will have exposure to high-quality work of a diverse range of well-known artists and designers from different communities through which they will utilise, develop and practise the following skills:
The school values of Love, Aspiration and Community are promoted through many opportunities such as our whole school ‘Arts Week’ which further explores a range of styles and techniques.
At Holy Trinity School we utilise sketch books from Reception to Year 6 to provide children with a space to practise and experiment with ideas and techniques prior to embarking on final pieces. Sketch books also allow children to look back and evaluate their own personal progress.
Painting
Sculpture
Printing
Textiles
Impact
The Art and Design curriculum develops the children’s awareness and love of The Arts. Children’s work is displayed around the school and extra curricular competitions allow further exploration while also raising the profile of the subject within our school community. We encourage children to express themselves creatively and also provide them with artistic vocabulary to better articulate their thoughts and feelings about art.
It is our aspiration that the skills and knowledge that children acquire in Art and Design, paired with a love and enjoyment of The Arts, will remain with our learners long after they leave Holy Trinity School community, allowing them to explore these avenues in the future either as career options or for their own personal enjoyment.
Love, Aspiration, Community

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing - Holy Trinity CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Computing
Computing Progression Map
Intent
At Holy Trinity School, we recognise the impact technology has in the everyday part of our lives, as such its use will play an essential and important part of our pupil’s home and work environments. Therefore, an awareness of the importance of educating our pupils on how to use technology positively, responsibly and safely is at the forefront of our consideration at Holy Trinity.
The new national curriculum for Computing has been developed to equip young people with the foundational skills, knowledge and understanding of computing that they will need throughout their lives, promoting a love for learning and encouraging a lifelong curiosity about the rapidly changing world of technology. In addition to implementing this, we aim to support our children to be responsible, enthusiastic, confident and creative users of information and communication technology (including desktop computers, laptops, tablets, programmable robots, cameras, and audio equipment).
Implementation
Each student at Holy Trinity has one hour of computing time every week. Children can use a variety of applications and software during these lessons to aid in learning a variety of crucial skills. Children will expand their understanding of digital systems and investigate how programming may be utilised to utilise this knowledge. In the process of resolving potential issues, children are encouraged to debug programmes and develop into independent learners. Our school also places a strong emphasis on teaching students digital literacy and giving them the tools they need to express themselves in positive, suitable and appropriate ways online, fostering a sense of respect and responsibility within both online and physical communities.
We use the NCCE Teach Computing scheme of work in order to ensure that all areas of the Computing Curriculum are being taught and carefully assessed. It is structured into units for each year group, and each unit is broken down into lessons. Units can generally be taught in any order, with the exception of programming, where concepts and skills rely on prior knowledge and experiences.
Online safety is one of the most crucial aspects of computing, for safeguarding purposes, and is covered with all students throughout all key stages. When using programmes or working online, children are taught how to spot suspicious or harmful content and how to act appropriately. For more information regarding Online Safety please visit our Keeping Safe Page.
Impact
The implementation of this aspirational curriculum is designed to ensure that when children leave Holy Trinity School, they are competent and safe users of ICT; with a foundational understanding of how technology works, a range of skills in how to creatively use digital media and an awareness of safe practise which they can carry with them to equip them for their next stage of education and beyond. To best embed and comprehend this, we encourage frequent conversations between teachers and students.
The impact of our curriculum will be best demonstrated by the way students present, distribute, celebrate, and publish their work. Reviewing students’ knowledge and skills is another way we look for evidence.
Love, Aspiration, Community

pageCache.text:
Design and Technology
DT Progression of skills
Intent
At Holy Trinity School, we acknowledge the impact that an interesting and engaging Design and Technology curriculum can have on a child’s development and their understanding of products in the world around them.
Design and Technology, as a practical subject, cultivates the values of love, aspiration, and community among children. It encourages students to express their creativity and imagination, fostering a deep love for the process of bringing a concept to life. As children embark on their design journey, they aspire to create meaningful and innovative products, while learning new skills. Through collaborative projects, a sense of community is grown, where students work together, share ideas, and support one another. In this way, Design and Technology not only builds practical skills but also instils the values of love for crafting, aspirations for excellence, and a strong sense of community among all our learners. Here they will utilise and develop the key skills associated with Design and Technology found within the broad categories of:
Implementation
Design and Technology at Holy Trinity School builds a culture of aspiration, love, and community, guiding students to create purposeful solutions that address real-life problems. Through a blend of creativity, imagination, and problem-solving, children embark on stimulating projects that not only cater to their individual needs but also resonate with the broader community. By crafting appealing and functional products within their year groups, students not only refine their design skills but also cultivate a sense of aspiration, aspiring to make a tangible difference in the world. This ethos is reinforced by our curriculum’s integration of knowledge from various subjects, such as mathematics, science, computing, and art, building students’ understanding of the connection of STEM subjects and fostering a love for learning and creating.
At Holy Trinity School children will use sketchbooks to design and plan their projects prior to making them. These allow children to make changes to plans along the way and look back on ideas in order to evaluate how successful they were and learn from this. Through study and evaluation of past and present design and technology, they will develop a critical understanding of its importance and impact on our everyday lives.
Impact
Encouraging resourcefulness and innovation, we equip students with essential skills for success in life beyond primary education. By showcasing and testing examples of children’s Design and Technology projects throughout the school, students can learning skills involved in in Design Technology and build on problem solving skill and learn about designs from the past and present.
Love, Aspiration, Community

pageCache.text:
Reading
Guided Reading progression map – updated Jan 2025
Guided Reading progression map specific to Nursery Literacy
Intent
At Holy Trinity our intent is to foster a community of readers who will be inspired to develop a love of reading through reading, enjoying and appreciating an aspirational variety of texts.
Our purpose is reading for meaning and enjoyment. We immerse children in a literary world through our text – rich reading curriculum, therefore creating strong levels of engagement to provide meaning and authentic contexts for primary English. Our children become critical readers as they encounter a wide-range of significant authors and a variety of fiction, non-fiction and poetry.Our aim is to develop fluency, expression and understanding of the text, as well as an enjoyment of books and a love of reading.
Implementation
Our woodland-themed library is located on the ground floor. It is a calm, inviting environment that promotes the love of reading for pleasure, with areas for small teaching groups and an extensive range of high-quality texts spanning a range of genres. We have different library areas which cater for EYFS, Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2. It is open regularly throughout the week for the children to visit.
Children will be read to everyday.
Impact
A strong reading profile is evident throughout the school, showcasing life-long lovers of reading. Children will have high expectations of themselves and experience pride, joy and sense of achievement when reading.
Writing
English writing progression of skills and knowledge 2024/25.
Intent
At Holy Trinity Primary School, we inspire our pupils to think and write innovatively, to be brave with their use of language, and write with clear purpose and pleasure. It is our aspiration to build a community of writers and foster a love of writing.
We believe it is important for our pupils’ futures to be able to write confidently in all contexts, so we create opportunities for children to develop a life-long love of writing, through an inclusive, diverse and creative writing curriculum. Our pupils develop spoken language through debate, drama and discussion about the issues raised in the texts. As a school, we value how our aspirational text choices can help expand our pupils’ knowledge beyond their immediate experiences and inspire their writing.
Implementation
To discover more about ‘The Write Stuff’ approach to writing, please click here: The Write Stuff
Impact
By the end of Year Six, children will be able to write clearly and accurately and adapt their language and style in and for a range of contexts, purposes and audiences. Our pupils will acquire a wide vocabulary and have a strong command of the written word. Most importantly, they will develop a strong sense of love for writing, become confident writers throughout their journey and be well equipped for the next stage of their education.
Spelling
Spelling Progression Map Year 2
Spelling Progression Map Year 3 & Year 4
Spelling Progression Map Year 5 & 6
Intent
At Holy Trinity Primary School, we inspire our pupils to think and write innovatively, to be brave with their use of language, and write with clear purpose and pleasure.
In order for these aims to be realised, it is essential that our pupils learn the knowledge and skills to spell accurately. Children who can spell feel confident and are able to write with satisfaction. We want our pupils to be equipped with the knowledge and range of strategies for learning to spell and to be able to apply their strategies when spelling words in their independent writing. We want to provide our pupils with opportunities to explore and investigate the English language.
Implementation
Building on the Read, Write, Inc. provision for phonics in EYFS and KS1, children in year groups 3 – 6 are taught the national spelling curriculum using the RWI spelling programme. This version has been adapted to suit the needs of the children at Holy Trinity Primary School. With the Read Write Inc. approach to the teaching of spellings we support and encourage children to become both confident and independent spellers which will help them to become better writers.
Our English curriculum provides many purposeful opportunities for spelling development. As children progress from RWI Phonics they begin to engage in RWI Spelling from spring of Year 2 through to Year 6 focussing on the National Curriculum spelling objectives. The spelling curriculum is mapped so that all rules and words are taught across cycle one then within cycle two, all rules are revisited to ensure they are embedded. Revisiting spelling patterns and rules regularly is key to them becoming successful spellers. Furthermore, regular consolidation sessions allow teachers and children to review previously taught spelling rules in a different context. Regular assessment opportunities take place across the year. At Holy Trinity, we hold spelling strategy lessons twice a week, which include two activity-based learning sessions focused on Phonics, Orthography, Morphology, and Etymology. These lessons are supported by resources such as Speed Charts, Speed Mats, Jotters, RWI Practice Books, and Dictionaries. After reviewing spelling strategies using keywords, students are shown how to apply these in their writing across the curriculum.
Our pupils acquire the knowledge and learn the skills to apply their spelling skills to a variety of purposes in a range of cross-curricular contexts. Our pupils are encouraged to think creatively, be adventurous with their use of language, and write with a clear purpose.
Please click here for the RWI Spelling Scheme overview on the Ruth Miskin website.
Impact
Children are assessed through spelling tests and the end of KS2 SATS examinations. Outcomes of written work further evidence the children’s confidence and accuracy in spelling across the school, alongside closed spelling tasks which test children’s knowledge and how well the spelling rules are embedded.
When spelling, our pupils:
In KS2 at Holy Trinity the children learn Latin. This greatly supports our learners with understanding the etymology of language and its roots and spellings. The links between English and Latin enthuse and inspire our community to explore further into the origins of English and develop a love for languages.
Handwriting
Handwriting Progression Map.
Intent
At Holy Trinity, we expect children to take pride in the presentation of their written work so we ensure that they are taught to have a neat, fluent and cursive handwriting style.
Implementation
We will deliver five weekly sessions beginning in the Early Years with early writing skills activities such as tracing letters and forming letters in shaving foam. We will progress onto our cursive script that prepares children to join their handwriting once they have developed their fine motor skills. Our aim for handwriting is to build a community of legible and fluent handwriters in all areas of the curriculum.
Impact
By Year 6, children’s handwriting will be clear, accurate and formed using the cursive script. This will be monitored by teachers when books are marked and within daily handwriting lessons. If the children take pride in their presentation it follows that they will take pride in the content and quality of their work.
Love, Aspiration, Community

Forest School
Intent
At Holy Trinity School our intent is to foster a community of knowledgeable young learners with a sense of responsibility to the natural world, who will be inspired to develop a love of the outdoors and nature, engaging and enjoying aspirational challenges that will enable them to ‘have a go’ and master new skills. We believe that through the inclusion of outdoor learning woven through all areas of the curriculum, we will best support the holistic development of each child.
We want our pupils to:
Develop a love of learning.
Implementation
Each half term every class at HT has a ‘Forest School session’, with a trained Forest School Leader. Rain or shine the children have opportunities to explore a variety of different outdoor areas and immerse themselves in different activities. These include:
We are extremely lucky to be located a short walk from both Richmond Park and Sheen Common and to have a wonderful woodland garden and pond area. We also run forest school nurture groups.
pond dipping in our outdoor learning area
creating art work and tree rubbings
building fires and making bread/toasting marshmallows
Impact
The impact of Outdoor Learning on learning will be focused on the knowledge and skills gained at the end of each key stage. Pupils will have/be able to:
Developed a confidence to try new activities.
Follow instructions involving several ideas/actions.
Love, Aspiration, Community

pageCache.text:
Geography
Geography Progression Map
Intent
At Holy Trinity School, our geography curriculum has been carefully planned and tailored in a way that encourages all children to develop their understanding of locational and place knowledge, human and physical geography and fieldwork. Our intent is to inspire the next generation to have a curiosity and passion for the world around them. In itself, geography plays a vital part of our curriculum and helps pupils to understand the complexity of our planet and appreciate the diversity of cultures that exists across continents.
As a multicultural school, we believe it is important to make children more aware of the different cultures of those around them. Geography also teaches our pupils how they are global citizens and provides them with the tools to be proactive when dealing with the human impacts on our planet such as climate change. The children will also learn to show compassion and love towards all cultures of the world. This links in with our core Christian values of love, aspiration and community.
The geography curriculum at Holy Trinity School has been expertly designed and has drawn upon a range of schemes and resources such as ‘The Royal Geographical Society.’ Our geography vision is to challenge all children in our community and promote aspiration in all lessons. In addition to this, all of our teaching materials have been carefully selected to reflect both our school community and locality in West London. For example, as well as studying the river defences along the River Thames, pupils will also find out about the Yangtze River in Asia and learn about the similarities and differences between them. There is an intrinsic link with our history curriculum and other subjects; this allows the learning to become more meaningful for the pupils. All geography lessons taught at Holy Trinity School provide an in-depth coverage of the national curriculum and individual units have been designed in a manner that gives pupils the best opportunity to progress across year groups.
The followings statements outline our intent for geography at Holy Trinity School:
in-depth coverage of the national curriculum
consultation of expert advice of geography associations
Implementation
Geography lessons at Holy Trinity School have been structured around the National Curriculum, taking into account the key concepts to ensure that the subject is taught in a spiral manner. The skills and knowledge explored and developed have been carefully planned and mapped out in our geography progression of skills map. Our students will make connections between different units and recap key vocabulary and events throughout their school journey. History and geography lessons are taught on alternate weeks and both subjects have been intrinsically designed to enable children to embed and retain skills, knowledge and vocabulary.
Children will experience geography through interactive and stimulating lessons and undertake field work relevant to their topics to bring their geography learning to life. We take full advantage of the amazing geographical sites within the local area to provide immersive experiences to engage and enthuse the children. We are extremely fortunate to be located in the geographically diverse region of West London. We want our pupils to have a deep understanding of their local surroundings and utilise the natural landmarks on their doorstep including: The River Thames, Kew Gardens and Richmond Park. For example, our year four pupils visit Kew Gardens where they use data loggers and weather instruments to compare the climate and weather patterns in the UK to that of the Amazon Rainforest. The data is then collated by the children and used to devise a range of comparative charts to further inform their learning.
Impact
The impact of our geography curriculum can be seen on a daily basis at Holy Trinity School. The children’s work, localised trips, outstanding teaching, engaging displays and pupil voice feedback are just some examples. Each pupil has a geography exercise book that travels up the school with them from year one to year six. This acts as a fantastic assessment tool that displays the progression of learning for every pupil. The impact is also measured through termly learning walks and gathering the children’s thoughts on geography during ‘Pupil Voice’ activities. By the time they leave Holy Trinity, pupils will have had the opportunity to analyse and compare regions from every corner of the world with their own local area.
Love, Aspiration, Community
